title: ChatGPT-using lawyer punished for citing fake testimony from made-up witnesses
raw_text: The New Mexico Supreme Court held a ChatGPT-using lawyer in direct contempt of court for submitting a brief with "false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses," including fake police testimony and other mistakes. The state's top court referred the lawyer to a disciplinary board for further proceedings and concluded that he "demonstrated a lack of remorse and a lack of concern for his client." Attorney Stephen Aarons "admitted to the Court that he did not verify the factual claims and legal authority in his AI-generated brief before signing it and filing it with the Court, and that he did not inform his client of this failure or that the brief in chief contained multiple factual and legal misrepresentations," the state Supreme Court said in an order on Wednesday. Aarons has been a criminal defense lawyer in New Mexico for over 40 years and was hired by a defendant's family members to appeal a murder conviction. Aaron's now-former client, Oscar Renee Sandoval, was sentenced to life in prison in February 2025 after being convicted of killing Shiereen Al-Jibury, who was his partner and the mother of his children. title: Scientists unlock secrets of ancient Egyptian materials with proteomics
raw_text: Credit: Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities, Stockholm Credit: Museum of Mediterranean and Near Eastern Antiquities, Stockholm The precise composition of ancient Egyptian paints, binders, adhesives, and similar materials used to make artifacts is largely unknown, in part because a full analysis would require taking samples that would damage those valuable artifacts. The development of cutting-edge, non-destructive techniques has been helping to unlock those secrets, aiding conservation efforts. Most recently, researchers have used mass spectrometry-based proteomics to analyze the glues and adhesives in a broad set of Egyptian artifacts, according to a new paper published in the journal Science Advances. They found plenty of expected sources, such as animal collagens and egg proteins, but also plant proteins, specifically from sesame and drumstick tree (moringa) cereals. As previously reported , the ancient Egyptians had a highly formalized (and easily recognizable) painting style, and there has been considerable interest in gaining insights into the specific pigments and painting techniques employed. Common pigments included hematite and realgar for red; goethite and orpiment for yellow; Egyptian blue; Egyptian green; carbon-based black; and calcite, gypsum, anhydrite, and huntite for white. raw_text: I wanted to share my side-project: gPTY. Started off as an idea to combine Godot and Rust in a project (two stacks I wanted to use more to learn more). The base inspiration was tmux - simply allow spawning multiple PTYs and then let the user grid/tile them how they see fit. But since we have the Godot game engine at our disposal, we can do some more interesting things, like add an FPS counter, and then subsequently also let people set their preferred FPS (the idea being the potential lower power draw if someone's running it on a laptop on battery power vs someone running it on a desktop with high/native FPS). In its current state, with me using Oh-my-Pi a lot, it's evolving into a terminal workspace that can be used for orchestrating autonomous AI agents by way of dogfooding (or you know, just run herdr inside of gPTY - it's the better orchestrator and just good software - I found it after starting this project, and now I'm finding myself using it a lot). Also, we're not limited to just terminals. Since we have Godot, we have basically a 2D (and potentially a 3D) canvas to play with. We can already full-screen the app for "zen" mode, no taskbar, no distractions. TUI die-hards can have their media or other apps entirely in terminal panes. title: ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral
raw_text: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic. Now the technique has become mainstream as attackers reap its simplicity and effectiveness in infecting users of PCs and Macs alike. All that’s required is a compromised website—a painless enough task—a fake CAPTCHA overlay, and the inclusion of a single terminal command. So many visitors get suckered into pasting and running the command that just about every malware pusher has adopted the technique. Even Kremlin-backed hacking groups are joining in. “Reddit is becoming post after post after post of people getting their computer infected via ClickFix,” independent researcher Kevin Beaumont observed Thursday . “Legit websites everywhere [are] getting hacked to serve the fake captcha prompts.” How many of us make things worse More seasoned Internet users—a fair number who read this site—are quick to dismiss the attack. They typically blame the people who fall for the scams and marvel at their gullibility and lack of attention. The reality is that for more casual users, using computers and the Internet has become so difficult—think impossible-to-close interstitials, CAPTCHAs with an endless series of pictures to analyze, and constantly changing interfaces that bury the features they’re looking for—that they have grown desensitized to instructions that seem ridiculous and burdensome. title: What happens when quantum mechanics and relativity meet?
raw_text: Almost a hundred years ago, physicists theorized out what free fall should do to a quantum wave. If the solution they came up with is wrong, quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory of gravity flatly contradict each other. But testing it has been impossible because nobody has managed to build an interferometer that could perform the necessary measurement. Now, a team led by Ron Folman, a physicist at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, with collaborators in Germany, the UK, and the US, including Nobel laureate Roger Penrose, has done it. They built a new interferometer that gives a single atom two possible paths at once: one that involves a free fall, and another where it is held perfectly still. Both paths end at the same place at the same moment, allowing the team to measure what the fall does to a wave-like property of the atom. Long time coming Ever since Galileo, physicists have known how to describe a falling object—where it is, how fast it goes, or how quickly it accelerates. Quantum mechanics, though, insists that every object is also a wave. “Every particle, doesn't matter if it's a car or a spaceship or an atom, is a wave,” Folman says. “Everything that is a wave, like sea waves or sound waves, goes up and down. And if you're up or down, this is measured by something called a phase. A phase just tells you if you are at the top of the wave or at the bottom.” Read full article Comments

title: Could United Launch Alliance's money problems finally force its owners to sell?
raw_text: Pretty much every rocket company in the United States, save one, has embraced two fundamental tenets: reusability and diversification. Most famously, SpaceX branched out from reusable rockets to pursue and dominate a growing spectrum of space services: cargo delivery, human spaceflight, satellite production, broadband, and, perhaps soon, orbital data centers and in-space manufacturing. Blue Origin is evolving from a pure rocket company into a satellite manufacturer, robotics developer, and, most recently, a potential competitor for SpaceX's Starlink network. Rocket Lab used a different approach to diversify after achieving success with its small Electron launch vehicle. The company relocated its headquarters from New Zealand to Southern California, started building spacecraft and payloads, and then went on a spree of corporate acquisitions to expand into satellite communications and take on a new role as a merchant supplier of satellite components and sensors. It's now in a stage of advanced development of its partially reusable next-generation Neutron launch vehicle. Read full article Comments

title: Bringing Big Ideas Home: Reflections from PLA 2026 in Minneapolis
raw_text: The most valuable takeaway from my time at the Public Library Association Conference wasn’t just new ideas; it was a renewed sense of purpose. As the director of a small, rural library in Elba, Alabama, I was thrilled to receive a PLA scholarship to attend the conference in Minneapolis. PLA has supported our library in meaningful ways over the years, including a 2019 grant that funded a high school intern. That student is now about to graduate from college and, inspired by her experience at our library, is pursuing her MLS. Moments like that are a powerful reminder of the long-term impact of library work. Energy, Inspiration, and Hard Conversations I attended with a colleague from a neighboring library, and from the moment we walked into the Minneapolis Convention Center, the energy was contagious. We immediately felt welcomed, not just by the upbeat registration staff but by the shared sense of purpose among attendees. The opening session set the tone. Hearing from speakers, including Bryan Stevenson, was both inspiring and challenging. His remarks encouraged me to reflect more deeply on local history in my own community, including the possibility of researching and acknowledging difficult chapters like lynchings. I left with a desire to partner with our local historical preservation group to explore ways to honor and remember those stories. raw_text: My name is Lana Sweeting, and I was lucky enough to be selected for a 2026 PLA scholarship. I serve as an Adult Reference Librarian in Portland, Oregon, where much of my work focuses on serving the Black community through programming, collections, and outreach. While there were many sessions that were relevant and helpful to my everyday work, two in particular invigorated my work as a public librarian. First, I felt very drawn to the session “Every Story Matters, Every Body Belongs: Fat Inclusive Libraries.” The presenter, Amelia Mason, was absolutely wonderful and very knowledgeable on the subject. I was locked in from the very first slide, which simply said, “I Am Fat.” The honest and positive energy went up from there. Along with sharing quantitative data, Amelia discussed myths surrounding fatness, as well as history, race, fat acceptance and neutrality, and how these issues apply to library spaces and other spaces we regularly occupy. For example, Amelia noted that PLA shirts on the website only went up to size 3XL. After the session, I felt informed and inspired to take this information back to Multnomah County Library. The session included a resource booklist that inspired me to create a booklist and display for my own library and begin conversations around diversity audits of our catalog so we can make relevant materials more accessible. title: The Future Is Now: Black Men in Libraries
raw_text: I appreciated the chance to attend the PLA 2026 Conference. As an early-career librarian and MLIS student at the University of South Florida, I had no idea what to expect, but I am proud to report that I was not let down. I came to Minneapolis with a strong desire to learn more about public libraries, and I did just that. I learned more about how to strengthen library boards and foundations, how to protect queer and trans staff, and how to provide library services to those who are incarcerated. I am really happy with my experience. I attended various community-related sessions because it is so important to build relationships and have a sense of belonging, especially in today’s tumultuous political climate. This is also important in my Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) journey, where I promote positive connections, encourage librarians to embrace diversity, and build relationships with those around them. PLA was an amazing conference filled with experts who were welcoming and eager to answer questions from the audience. It was difficult to choose just one program to highlight because I genuinely enjoyed all the sessions. However, one stood out to me. My favorite was Black Men in Libraries: Our History, Our Heroes, and Our Horizon . raw_text: September 2026 Drie veelgestelde vragen uitgelicht Op de websites van Digisterker, DigiVitaler en DigiVeiliger vind je antwoorden op veelgestelde vragen over de lesprogramma’s. Hoe kan ik de Digisterker Docenten Demo inzetten tijdens de les? - Digisterkervraag, docent De Digisterker Docenten Demo is een hulpmiddel dat u kunt gebruiken tijdens de les. In de Docenten Demo staat een stappenplan en de bijbehorende schermafbeeldingen van een website. Met behulp van de Demo kunt u de website bij het betreffende onderwerp uitleggen. Er zijn een aantal manieren waarop u deze kunt gebruiken tijdens de les: Demonstratie van alle stappen: bespreek alle stappen in één keer en laat de cursisten oefenen met alle stappen. Demonstratie per stap: bespreek de volledige stap en laat cursisten daarna oefenen met deze stap. Demonstratie per afbeelding: bespreek elke afbeelding apart en laat cursisten steeds oefenen per afbeelding. Gedeeltelijke demonstratie op de website: laat eerst de echte website zien en gebruik de Demo vanaf het moment dat u moet inloggen met DigiD. title: Digisterker-Nieuwsbrief
raw_text: September 2026 Vernieuwde tool voor DigiVitaler-certificaten Na afloop van een DigiVitaler-cursus kun je cursisten een persoonlijk certificaat meegeven. De tool waarmee docenten deze certificaten kunnen maken, is vernieuwd. Hierdoor gaat het maken van de certificaten een stuk eenvoudiger. In de vernieuwde tool vul je de namen van de cursisten in en selecteer je welke DigiVitaler-lessen zij hebben gevolgd. Vervolgens voeg je de plaats, datum, naam van de organisatie en de naam van de docent toe. Ook kun je het logo van je eigen organisatie uploaden. Heb je meerdere deelnemers, dan kun je hun namen in één keer invoeren. Je ontvangt vervolgens één pdf-bestand, met voor iedere deelnemer een persoonlijk certificaat op een aparte pagina. Direct zien hoe het certificaat eruitziet Een handige verbetering is dat je tijdens het invullen direct een voorbeeld van het certificaat ziet. Wijzig je iets? Dan wordt het voorbeeld automatisch aangepast. Zo kun je meteen zien of alle gegevens goed staan en hoe het uiteindelijke certificaat eruitziet. Ben je tevreden met het resultaat? Dan download je de certificaten als pdf. De vernieuwde tool is te vinden op dezelfde plek als voorheen.

raw_text: September 2026 Aan de slag met DigiVeiliger? Dat kan nu ook met een bibliotheeklicentie Afgelopen maart lanceerden we DigiVeiliger – zeker online , ons lesprogramma voor volwassenen over digitale veiligheid. De belangstelling vanuit bibliotheken is groot. Voor de DigiVeiliger-Startersregeling, waarmee bibliotheken een jaar lang kosteloos ervaring kunnen opdoen met het programma, ontvingen we veel aanmeldingen. Inmiddels zijn 15 bibliotheken geselecteerd om DigiVeiliger te gaan gebruiken. Ook andere bibliotheken willen DigiVeiliger graag inzetten. We kregen regelmatig de vraag: kunnen we zelf een licentie aanschaffen? Met de DigiVeiliger-Volgersregeling maken we dat nu mogelijk. DigiVeiliger-Volgersregeling Met de Volgersregeling kunnen bibliotheken DigiVeiliger opnemen in hun aanbod voor inwoners in hun werkgebied. Een bibliotheeklicentie kost € 1.500 per licentiejaar. Daarmee krijgt de bibliotheekorganisatie onder andere toegang tot de DigiVeiliger-docenteninstructie voor medewerkers en vrijwilligers, actueel lesmateriaal en ondersteunende materialen voor docenten en coördinatoren. Betrek lokale partners Digitale veiligheid is een onderwerp dat vaak ook leeft bij lokale partners, zoals gemeenten en politie. Het kan daarom interessant zijn om met hen te verkennen hoe DigiVeiliger aansluit bij gezamenlijke ambities rond de digitale weerbaarheid van inwoners. title: ALA Launches Reporting Form for Incidents Against Immigrants in Libraries
raw_text: Acknowledgments: The author thanks Hayley Park of the University of Maryland for her contributions to language used in this article and Derek Wilmott of the University of Toledo for his assistance in developing the incident reporting form. Libraries across the country are navigating heightened immigration enforcement activity while trying to support community members and staff. Library leaders may face difficult decisions about how to respond to enforcement activity, address harassment, communicate with their communities, and protect patrons and employees, often with limited information about what other libraries are experiencing. Consider a public library responding to increased immigration enforcement activity in its community. Library leadership might consider issuing a public statement supporting immigrants but ultimately decide against it after consulting legal counsel, concerned that doing so could make the library a target. How can library leaders make decisions like this when much of the information available to them comes from anecdotal experiences or informal conversations with colleagues? Better data can help. The Services to Refugees, Immigrants, and Displaced Persons (SRIDP) Subcommittee is proud to announce the launch of the Incidents Against Immigrants in Libraries reporting form .
